note: The Treaty of Verdun (843) — signed after three years of Carolingian civil war following Louis the Pious's death — permanently divided the Carolingian Empire among his three surviving sons: Louis the German (East Francia/Germany), Charles the Bald (West Francia/France), and Lothair (Middle Francia + the imperial title). The partition created the political geography of Western Europe: France and Germany as separate states, with the contested 'middle strip' (Lorraine, Burgundy, Italy) as the perpetual battleground between them for the next 1,100 years.

_quarry.structural_significance: Creates the fundamental political geography of modern Western Europe; France and Germany emerge as distinct states; the 'Middle Francia' corridor — Lorraine, Burgundy, the Low Countries, northern Italy — becomes the most contested territory in European history
